title: ManifestResponse
description: Complete command tree for an agent to discover all available commands, their flags, exit codes, contracts, and examples in a single call, without iterating --help per subcommand.

schema_version.description: Contract version of this ManifestResponse, 3.x for this schema. A consumer reads it before anything else: from 3.0 on, global options live in the root flags map, not in each CommandEntry.flags.

framework_version.description: Version of the CLI framework or tool binary.

etag.description: Stable content hash of the manifest. Changes only when command registrations change. Agents pass this back via --etag to receive a cache hit instead of recomputing the full manifest.

commands.description: Flat map from dot-separated command path to CommandEntry. 'deploy.rollback' is the rollback subcommand of deploy. Every registered command appears here, including built-ins.

dependencies.description: External runtime dependencies the tool declares (REQ-O-031). tool doctor checks each entry.

flags.description: Global options: flags every command accepts, before or after the command path, keyed by flag name without leading --. A CommandEntry.flags map never repeats a name or short alias listed here. Only the format flag may carry media_types. Sourced from REQ-F-079.

format.description: The --format flag (REQ-O-001); the only flag that may carry media_types.

exit_codes.description: Shared exit-code table every command inherits. A CommandEntry.exit_codes lists only codes absent from this table or whose entry differs; the command's effective table is this map overlaid with its own. Hoisting the framework codes here keeps the manifest small for agents that read it whole.

env_vars.description: Environment variables the tool reads that back no flag and supply no secret, such as TOOL_DEBUG or TOOL_AUDIT_LOG, each with a description. A name without the tool prefix immediately follows the entry for the same setting's tool-prefixed name, which the tool reads first. A name here appears nowhere else in the manifest: a variable that supplies a flag's value is listed only in that FlagEntry.env_vars, and a secret only in a secret_env_vars or token_env_vars. Universal names such as NO_COLOR or HOME are not listed. Sourced from REQ-F-073.

secret_env_vars.description: Environment variable names that supply a secret every command reads, such as a tool-wide API key; never a value or a default. A name here appears in no CommandEntry.secret_env_vars and no FlagEntry.env_vars; each command's effective secrets are these plus its own. Sourced from REQ-F-073 and REQ-C-016.

description.description: One-sentence summary of what the command does.

aliases.description: Alternative names this command can be invoked with.

danger_level.description: Mutation risk level. safe: read-only, no side effects on state (writes only cache, log, temp, or output paths); mutating: creates or modifies state; destructive: permanently deletes or irreversibly modifies state. Sourced from REQ-C-002.

idempotent.description: True when a repeat with the same arguments converges on the same state, whatever a previous attempt left behind. A non-retryable exit whose ExitCodeEntry declares side_effects partial is then recovered by rerunning the identical command without inspecting state. Absent means false; redundant on a safe command. Distinct from --idempotency-key, which deduplicates one request. Sourced from REQ-C-002.

required_scopes.description: Minimal permission strings the command needs from the active credential, most critical first. Empty when no auth is required. Sourced from REQ-C-029.

flags.description: Command-local flags: map from flag name (without leading --) to FlagEntry. Global options live in the root flags map and are never repeated here; no local flag carries media_types. Sourced from REQ-C-015.

positionals.description: Positional arguments in the order they are given after the command path. Absent or empty when the command takes none. Only the last entry may be variadic. Sourced from REQ-C-015.

exit_codes.description: Map from exit code integer (as string key) to ExitCodeEntry. Sourced from REQ-C-001. When the manifest has a root exit_codes table, this map holds only the command's additions and overrides; tool <cmd> --schema always prints the effective table in full.

output_schema.description: JSON Schema draft-07 object describing the shape of the command's data payload on success. Agents use this to validate responses and detect schema drift. Sourced from REQ-C-015.

output_formats.description: Format values accepted by --format beyond the framework defaults (json, jsonl, tsv, plain). Omit when only defaults are supported. Sourced from REQ-O-049.

output_media_types.description: Map from a --format value this command accepts to the media type it writes, overriding the root format flag's media_types for this command. Required for each output_formats value outside the spec's format table and the root media_types. Sourced from REQ-O-049.

examples.description: Complete invocations that demonstrate the command. Agents copy these verbatim as starting points.

subcommands.description: Dot-separated paths of direct child commands. Resolve each via the top-level commands map.

builtin.description: True when the framework registers the command itself rather than the application, such as manifest or doctor. A built-in's subcommands are also true; an application command that replaces a built-in's name is false. Sourced from REQ-O-041.

output_file.description: Present exactly when the command registers --output <path>; absent means no --output. formatted: the file gets the --format representation of the result. binary: the file gets the raw bytes of a binary result and data describes the write as path, bytes, content_type, sha256; --output - exits 2. handler: the command handler writes the file and the command's own documentation describes its contents. envelope: the framework writes the final ResponseEnvelope as JSON to the file whatever --format selects; --format shapes only stdout. Sourced from REQ-O-001.

output_file_base.description: Directory a relative --output path resolves against; an absolute path is used as given. Present only when output_file is; absent means cwd. cwd: the working directory of the invocation. project_root: the project root the tool resolves for the invocation, whatever the working directory. resource: the directory of the resource the command acts on, as its description states. Sourced from REQ-O-001.

stdin.description: How the command reads stdin: buffered whole, or line by line as plain lines or typed records. Sourced from REQ-F-054 and REQ-O-004.

arguments.description: declared: the framework parses the command's arguments from its flags and positionals. passthrough: every token after the command path goes verbatim to another tool's parser, which owns stdout and the exit code; the final envelope is the last line of stderr, a non-zero delegated code gives error.code DELEGATED_EXIT, option_placement is strict, danger_level is never destructive, and confirm_flag is absent. Sourced from REQ-C-031.

help_argv.description: Passthrough commands only: the argv forwarded to the delegated tool in place of a lone --help or -h after the command path. Absent means the lone token is forwarded unchanged. Sourced from REQ-C-031.

stderr.description: child_log: stderr carries a wrapped program's output as plain text, line by line, regardless of --format and verbosity; --quiet silences it and stdout carries only the envelope. Absent means stderr carries the framework's own diagnostics only. Never on a passthrough command. Sourced from REQ-F-038.

stdout.description: protocol: the command serves the long-lived protocol named in protocol over stdio, so stdout is the protocol channel from the first byte and never carries a ResponseEnvelope; a failure before serving begins goes to stderr, in JSON mode as an envelope on its last line, with a declared exit code, and exit 0 means a clean shutdown such as stdin end-of-file. Absent means stdout carries envelopes. Sourced from REQ-C-032.

protocol.description: Name of the protocol the command serves on stdin and stdout, in lowercase kebab-case: mcp-stdio (Model Context Protocol over stdio), lsp (Language Server Protocol), dap (Debug Adapter Protocol), or another protocol's name in the same form. Present exactly when stdout is protocol. Sourced from REQ-C-032.

mcp.description: false: the tool's own MCP server never offers the command as a tool, such as an approval a person gives, a project-creating init, or a watch loop that never returns; an agent runs it through the CLI or hands it to a person. Present only when false; absent means the tool's MCP server may offer the command as a tool. Sourced from REQ-C-032.

option_placement.description: any: global options may appear anywhere and local options anywhere after the command path, including among positionals. strict: every option, global or local, must precede the first positional because everything from the first positional on is forwarded verbatim; -- also ends option parsing. Sourced from REQ-C-027.

interactive.description: True if the command may prompt for input in a TTY context; --yes and --non-interactive are then registered. Sourced from REQ-C-005.

has_network_io.description: True if the command makes outbound network connections or long blocking I/O calls; --timeout is then registered. Sourced from REQ-C-012.

steps.description: Ordered step names a multi-step command executes. Responses report completed, failed, and skipped steps by these names. Sourced from REQ-C-008.

spawns_background_process.description: True if the command starts a child process that outlives the invocation. Sourced from REQ-C-010.

cleanup_command.description: Exact command that stops the background process this command starts. Sourced from REQ-C-010.

max_lifetime_seconds.description: Maximum seconds the background process runs before the framework may terminate it. Sourced from REQ-C-010.

filesystem_side_effects.description: Every filesystem location the command may write to. Sourced from REQ-C-011.

secret_env_vars.description: Environment variable names that supply secret values for this command, beyond the root secret_env_vars every command reads. A secret is never a flag value, so these names never appear in FlagEntry.env_vars. Sourced from REQ-C-016.

platform.description: Supported operating system names such as linux or darwin. Absent means all platforms. Sourced from REQ-C-018.

required_tools.description: External binaries the command invokes, mapped to the minimum version each needs, or to * when any version will do: the binary need only resolve on PATH and is never run to read a version. Sourced from REQ-C-018.

subprocess.description: How the command builds arguments for a child binary. Sourced from REQ-C-019.

headless_supported.description: Auth commands only: true when the command can authenticate in non-TTY mode without a pre-acquired token. Sourced from REQ-C-021.

token_env_vars.description: Auth commands only: environment variables that supply a pre-acquired token. Required when headless_supported is false. A name here is not repeated in this command's secret_env_vars. Sourced from REQ-C-021 and REQ-F-073.

async.description: True when the command returns a job descriptor instead of waiting for completion. Sourced from REQ-C-022.

job_descriptor_schema.description: JSON Schema for the job descriptor returned in data by an async command. Sourced from REQ-C-022.

requires_editor.description: True when the command opens $EDITOR or $VISUAL unless an alternative flag is supplied. Sourced from REQ-C-023.

non_interactive_alternatives.description: Flag names, without leading --, that bypass the editor. Required when requires_editor is true. Sourced from REQ-C-023.

gui_operations.description: Display operations the command performs, such as browser_open or desktop_notification. Sourced from REQ-C-024.

headless_behavior.description: How gui_operations behave in headless mode. Sourced from REQ-C-024.

config_write_scope.description: Scope of configuration files the command may write. Sourced from REQ-C-025.

requires.description: Conditional argument dependency rules, evaluated in order. Sourced from REQ-C-026.

streaming_default.description: True when the command streams JSONL by default; --no-stream returns a single envelope. Sourced from REQ-O-004.

safe_default.description: True when the command runs in dry-run mode unless --live is passed. Sourced from REQ-O-048.

confirm_flag.description: Name, without leading --, of a boolean flag of the command or root that confirms execution. Without it the command previews under the dry-run contract (would_* effect, meta.dry_run true, exit 0, no side effects); with it the command runs. --dry-run wins over it. Only on mutating or destructive commands, never with safe_default true. Sourced from REQ-O-048.

type.description: Type of the flag value. object: one JSON object passed as a single argv token of JSON text, its shape declared in schema.

required.description: True if the flag must be provided for the command to proceed.

description.description: What the flag controls, including valid range or format constraints.

default.description: Value used when the flag is omitted. Omit this property (do not set null) when there is no default.

enum_values.description: Exhaustive list of accepted values. Present only when type is 'enum'.

short.description: Single-character shorthand (e.g. 'n' for --dry-run). Omit if none exists.

pattern.description: Anchored regular expression the value must match. Mutually exclusive with pattern_type. Sourced from REQ-C-020.

pattern_type.description: Built-in validation preset for resource identifiers. Mutually exclusive with pattern. Sourced from REQ-C-020.

env_vars.description: Environment variables the flag reads when it is not passed, in precedence order: the first one set wins, and a passed flag beats them all. A list that holds a name without the tool prefix also holds the tool-prefixed name, first. Never lists a secret; secrets are declared in CommandEntry.secret_env_vars. Sourced from REQ-F-073.

schema.description: JSON Schema draft-07 of one value: the object itself when type is object, one item when type is array. Required when type is object; present otherwise only when type is array. Sourced from REQ-C-015.

media_types.description: Root format flag only: map from each enum value to the media type it writes. Required for every value outside the spec's format table, optional for the spec's values, and every key is one of enum_values. Sourced from REQ-O-001.

MediaTypeMap.description: Map from a --format value to the media type that value writes, as a lowercase type/subtype without parameters such as text/html. Sourced from REQ-O-001.

name.description: Exact environment variable name, such as TOOL_PROJECT.

deprecated.description: True when the variable is still read but slated for removal; set a non-deprecated name instead.

description.description: What the variable controls and the values it accepts. Required on root env_vars entries, optional on a flag's, where the flag's description applies.

name.description: Name used in help and errors. Never typed by the caller; position alone identifies the argument.

required.description: True if the argument must be given. An optional positional never precedes a required one.

description.description: What the argument selects, including valid range or format constraints.

enum_values.description: Exhaustive list of accepted values. Required when type is 'enum'.

variadic.description: True if the argument takes every remaining value. Allowed on the last entry only.

StdinDeclaration.description: How the command reads stdin. Present when the command declares stdin input; --input-file <path> is then registered and reads the same way. Sourced from REQ-F-054 and REQ-O-004.

mode.description: buffered: stdin is read whole before the handler runs, up to max_bytes. lines: the handler reads one line at a time as it asks, with no total cap and each line up to max_line_bytes. records: lines mode where each line is one JSON record checked against record_schema and the stream ends on a _summary line.

max_bytes.description: Total stdin cap in bytes for buffered mode; TOOL_MAX_STDIN_BYTES overrides it at run time. Absent means 65536. Sourced from REQ-F-054.

max_line_bytes.description: Cap in bytes on one line, line terminator excluded, for lines and records mode. Absent means 1048576. Sourced from REQ-F-054.

record_schema.description: JSON Schema draft-07 object one record must match in records mode. Compare it with a producer's output_schema item type before piping. Sourced from REQ-O-004.

description.description: One-line description of what this example demonstrates.

command.description: Full invocation string an agent can use verbatim.

path.description: Template or glob for paths the command writes.

type.description: Category of the side effect. output is a path the command writes as its product (a report, a rendered page, collected evidence): status lists it, cleanup never removes it, and it takes neither ttl_seconds nor clearable_with. A per-call --output path is declared by output_file instead.

ttl_seconds.description: Seconds until the path is considered stale. Omit when permanent.

clearable_with.description: Exact command that removes this path.

user_controlled_args.description: Flag names whose values are passed to the child process as arguments.

hardcoded_args.description: Argument fragments the framework always passes verbatim.

ConditionalRule.description: One conditional argument dependency. Exactly one of the five shapes applies. A flag is present when the caller supplies it; neither a declared default nor a boolean given as false makes it present.

if_flag.description: Flag whose value triggers the rule.

if_value.description: Value of if_flag that makes then_required mandatory; compared as a value, so false matches a boolean given as false.

if_flag.description: Flag whose presence triggers the rule.

prohibited.description: Flags that are forbidden when if_flag is present; a boolean given as false, here or as if_flag, is not present.

if_flag.description: Flag whose absence triggers the rule.

default.description: Default applied to target_flag when if_flag is absent; a boolean if_flag given as false counts as absent.

any_of.description: Flags of which at least one must be present; neither a declared default nor a boolean given as false counts as present.

one_of.description: Flags of which exactly one must be present; neither a declared default nor a boolean given as false counts as present.

name.description: Dependency name, such as terraform or node.

check_command.description: Exact command that prints the installed version.

version_regex.description: Regular expression whose first group extracts the version from check_command output.

fix_command.description: Exact command that installs or upgrades the dependency.
